messages:
Priya K (FP&A): Thanks everyone — quick follow-up from today's all-hands finance section. I'm collecting the list of questions about FY25 cost prioritization, vendor onboarding timelines, and PO thresholds so leadership can respond here.
Jon (Eng Manager): Thanks — for the new router project, should we still assume the $250k cap from last quarter or push for a phased spend? unsure what to budget for now.
Marta (Product): Also curious — if we pause a feature rollout, do we reallocate that budget automatically to infra or does it go back to central pool?
Olivia (Finance Ops): Short answer: temporary holds revert to central until reallocation is approved. For vendor onboarding, current SLA is ~10 business days once the PO is raised and vendor info is complete.
Aisha (CFO): High level guidance: keep FY25 requests conservative. We want to preserve runway flexibility while funding critical ops. Specifics:
- Strategic projects (customer revenue impact / regulatory) get priority.
- Discretionary product experiments should be scoped smaller and staged.
- For the router project: please split into Phase A (MVP, ~60% scope) and Phase B (optional). Submit two PO line items with phase labels.
Jon (Eng Manager): Got it. For Phase A, can we do an accelerated approval if it's under $40k?
Olivia (Finance Ops): Approval tiers:
- <= $10,000: auto-approve via budget system
- > $10,000 and <= $50,000: FP&A review
- > $50,000: FP&A + Finance Ops review + exec signoff
Ravi (Legal): Note — any vendor contract > 1 year or with data-processing must pass Legal. That can add ~3-5 business days.
Priya K (FP&A): To add: when you submit a request, include expected ROI or metrics and the fallback plan. That speeds reviews.
Aisha (CFO): Example PO flow (paste into the ticket):
```text
1) Create PO request in Confluence -> attach vendor details
2) Select cost center + projected start/end
3) If amount <= 10k -> auto approve
4) Else -> FP&A assigns reviewer -> review window 3 business days
5) If contract terms flagged -> Legal intake -> 3-5 days
6) Finance Ops issues PO and notifies procurement
```
Marta (Product): Thanks Aisha — will do the phased PO. Do we have guidance on using reserved vs on-demand infra for Dedicated testing?
Aisha (CFO): Use reserved capacity only for long-lived, predictable throughput. For short tests, use on-demand / short-term credits. We'll provide a one-off testing credit pool for teams doing proofs of concept; submit a request and tag it "test-credit".
Jon (Eng Manager): Perfect. Anything special for vendor onboarding for open-source infra vendors? (no commercial license, just support contract)
Ravi (Legal): Support contracts still need vendor intake (KYC + liability review). We can expedite if vendor has standard SOC2 and public company status. Raise intake early.
Olivia (Finance Ops): I'll make a checklist template for PO requests and vendor intake and post it in #eng and #product by EOD tomorrow.
budget-bot: Reminder: monthly spend snapshots posted — new FY25 baseline will go live next Monday.
Priya K (FP&A): Thank you all. I'll collate here and send a follow-up doc with templates and the phased-PO example. If you have urgent items DM me :mailbox_with_mail:
Jon (Eng Manager): Appreciate it. :thumbsup:
Marta (Product): Thanks — will route the router Phase A PO today.
Aisha (CFO): Quick closing note: if teams have runway-impacting hires planned, flag them in the headcount review before budget reallocation. We'll prioritize essential roles.
Olivia (Finance Ops): Posted checklist here when ready: https://confluence.redwood/procurement/checklist (will include PO template)
Priya K (FP&A): Thread closed for new major asks after EOD Friday; minor clarifications ok to continue here.
Olivia (Finance Ops): Closing action: I’ll attach the checklist and the approval matrix to the all-hands notes.
